review.use_summary: Used MR-MEGA0.2 with three ancestry axes for multi-ancestry Parkinson disease meta-regression across seven cohorts, distinguished ancestry-related from residual heterogeneity, and used reported per-variant lnBF values for downstream locus fine-mapping.
review.implementation_scope_note: The study analyzed variants present in at least six of seven cohorts and explicitly applied no genomic control before meta-analysis. Native MR-MEGA0.2 ingestion, three-axis inference, source cohort admission, heterogeneity tests and lnBF are available through mrmega-tools. CrossMap hg19 harmonization, imputation/MAF/autosomal filters and the separate PLINK random-effects analysis remain distinct. Downstream locus-normalized Bayes-factor posterior/credible-set construction, reported significance conditions and MHC/MAPT exclusion are separate from the regression output. Complete paper commands, cohort effect/CI encoding and the exact historical binary are not frozen; no whole-paper reproduction is claimed.

review.use_summary: Used MR-MEGA0.2 for cross-ancestry meta-regression with four multidimensional-scaling ancestry axes, then recalculated P values from chi-square statistics because the original probability calculation did not support very small P values.
review.implementation_scope_note: The four-axis MR-MEGA0.2 analysis is separate from the preceding METAL fixed-effect analyses. Do not infer two aggregate input cohorts from EAS/EUR labels. Native mrmega-tools supports four inferred axes and retains raw/adjusted chi-square and degree fields; explicitly named stable native survival probabilities are independently R-tested and do not overwrite original approximation fields. Exact paper cohort inputs, GC flags, source binary and recalculation code are unstated; the current tested workflow does not establish historical file or whole-paper reproduction.

review.use_summary: Used MR-MEGA to examine index-variant effect heterogeneity attributable to ancestry rather than residual effects; six index variants showed significant ancestry-related heterogeneity.
review.implementation_scope_note: The source does not specify the MR-MEGA edition, ancestry-axis count, complete input/test family, command or GC settings. The six significant index variants are reported findings, not evidence that only those variants were tested. Native mrmega-tools supports separate ancestry and residual tests with explicit supplied/inferred axes, but does not infer those missing paper settings or variant population. The adjacent SuSiEx credible-set analysis is separate and must not be attributed to MR-MEGA.
